pageProps.description: How to fix the 'OS file watch limit reached' error when running yarn dev by increasing the Linux inotify file watch limit
pageProps.content:
##  OS file watch limit reached
When running `yarn run dev` (or `npm run dev`), you may encounter the following error.
```sh
{
    "title": "OS file watch limit reached error"
}
---
$ yarn run dev
...
Caused by: - OS file watch limit reached
```
```adcard
```
### Cause
This error occurs when the Linux kernel's <mark>inotify</mark> file watch limit is exceeded.

Development servers like Next.js, Vite, and Webpack simultaneously watch a large number of files in your project to detect changes and perform <mark>Hot Reload</mark>.  
If the default value of `fs.inotify.max_user_watches` is too low, the number of files to watch exceeds the limit and the error occurs.
```sh
{
    "title": "Check current inotify watch limit"
}
---
$ cat /proc/sys/fs/inotify/max_user_watches
8192
```
### Solution
You can resolve this by increasing the `fs.inotify.max_user_watches` value using `sysctl`.

First, apply it immediately to the current session.
```sh
{
    "title": "Apply immediately (current session)"
}
---
$ sudo sysctl fs.inotify.max_user_watches=524288
$ sudo sysctl -p
```
Add a permanent setting to `/etc/sysctl.conf` to persist the change across reboots.
```sh
{
    "title": "Persist across reboots"
}
---
$ echo fs.inotify.max_user_watches=524288 | sudo tee -a /etc/sysctl.conf
$ sudo sysctl -p
```
